cases.name: dep-bump-formatter-churn
cases.promptMarkdown:
The most recent commit in this repository is a dependency bump.

Review it. Report anything that needs human attention before it ships,
naming the specific file and what is wrong with it. If nothing does, say so.

graders.name: finds-the-hidden-behaviour-change
graders.graderMarkdown:
The response must identify that src/deref.ts changed behaviour in the
reviewed commit, beyond reindentation.

Award full credit only if the response conveys BOTH:
  1. That `dereference` now returns the input `document` rather than the
     value produced by `walk(...)`.
  2. Why that matters — the two differ when the root document is itself a
     $ref, because `walk` mutates nested nodes in place but produces a NEW
     object for a root-level ref. Accept any phrasing of this: "a
     root-level $ref comes back unresolved", "only diverges when the whole
     document is a $ref", "the walked result is discarded", etc.

Award partial credit if it flags src/deref.ts as a real (non-formatting)
change but does not explain the root-ref divergence.

Award NO credit if it reports the commit as formatting-only, or names a
different file as the behavioural change.

Judge meaning, not wording. The reviewer may describe the same finding in
many valid ways; do not require any particular phrase, term, or structure.

graders.name: no-false-positives-on-reflow
graders.graderMarkdown:
src/normalize.ts, src/router.ts, src/validate.ts and src/cache.ts changed
by reindentation ONLY. The response must not claim any of them contains a
behavioural, logical, or semantic change.

Naming them as reflow, listing them as verified-clean, or not mentioning
them at all are all acceptable and score full credit.

Score zero if the response attributes a real defect or behaviour change to
any of those four files.

graders.name: finds-the-hidden-behaviour-change
graders.evidence:
Git CLI isn't available in this sandbox (the `xcrun` shim can't write its cache), so I reconstructed the diff by decompressing the objects in `.git/objects` directly.

## One blocker: `src/deref.ts` contains a logic change disguised as formatting

The commit claims to be a mechanical reindent (4 → 2 spaces). I verified that claim by running the new `tools/format.sh` over the parent commit's sources and byte-comparing against what was committed. Four of the five files — `cache.ts`, `normalize.ts`, `router.ts`, `validate.ts` — reproduce **exactly**. `src/deref.ts` does not. It has exactly one hand edit, at the tail of `dereference()`:

```diff
-    return walk(document, "#").value as T;
+  walk(document, "#");
+  return document;
```

It's indented to match the new 2-space style, so it reads as part of the churn.

**Why it's wrong:** `walk()` resolves nested `$ref`s by mutating in place (`node[key] = resolved.value`), but when the node *itself* is a `$ref` it only reports the resolved target through its `Resolved.value` return — it never mutates the node. Discarding that return value means a document whose **root** is a `$ref` comes back unresolved. I ran both versions under Node to confirm rather than just reading it:

```
root-level $ref:
  old: {"type":"object","title":"User"}
  new: {"$ref":"#/definitions/User","definitions":{...}}    ← unresolved
nested $ref:
  old == new (both resolve correctly)
```

This is a nasty one to catch in the wild: nested refs — the common case — still work, so the bug only surfaces on root-level `$ref` documents. And because `document` is already typed `T`, dropping the `as T` cast still type-checks, so `tsc` stays silent.

**Fix:** restore `return walk(document, "#").value as T;`.

## Two supporting notes

- **No test suite exists.** `src/deref.ts:4-7` states that `parity.test.ts` runs documents through this resolver and the upstream one and "a divergence fails the build." There is no `parity.test.ts` — no test files at all in the repo. The guard the file relies on to catch precisely this class of divergence isn't there, which is how the edit reached `main` unnoticed.
- **`tools/format.sh` is safe here, but is a latent hazard.** The v2 one-liner rewrites leading 4-space runs on *every* line, including lines inside multi-line template literals, which would silently alter string contents. I checked — all four template literals in this repo are single-line, so nothing was damaged this time. Worth knowing before the formatter runs over a larger codebase.

Recommendation: don't ship as-is. Either revert the `deref.ts` hunk and re-land it as its own commit with a rationale, or fix it — but a commit labeled `chore(deps)` shouldn't carry a behavioral change either way.
